clue.text: Moulding young explorer in European parliament

indicators.note: in says the explorer is placed within the parliament's name

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament, in Europe
Dora the Explorer is a children's cartoon heroine

explanation.surface: A child adventurer turns up in the debating chamber of the European Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail is Ireland's parliament, so 'European' is fair; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado rail is a strip of wooden trim fixed along a wall at waist height, a type of moulding.

clue.text: Lawyer would liberate discharged lag

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

indicators.note: discharged means emptied, so each word loses its inside and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A solicitor intends to get a released convict set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' empties 'would' and 'liberate', leaving WD and LE. 'Lag' looks like a convict (British slang, old lag) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind by moving slowly, which is what dawdling means.

clue.text: Hairy? Leads to dermal abrasion with plastic surgeon

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, taken from each of the next two words
plastic means mouldable, so the letters of the word surgeon are reshaped

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon's skin-scraping procedure is shown as a worrying business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' turns SURGEON into NGEROUS. 'Hairy' is informal for risky, hence the question mark; it looks like a remark about skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a hairy situation is a frightening, risky one, a slang synonym for perilous.

clue.text: Strip in serif lettering

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A typographer spots a stripe within serif letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack it, stripping it of valuables.

clue.text: Is run out after batting has collapsed

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come behind the word for batting

parts.note: a cricket side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: a batsman's run-out after the innings has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IS RUN into RUINS. In cricket a batsman is out when dismissed; 'out' here is only the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in ruins has fallen down and been wrecked, so the phrase describes what has collapsed.

clue.text: Oddly missing maypole dancing mob's confidence

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of the word keeps its even ones
dancing means moving around, so the letters of mob are jumbled

explanation.surface: The crowd dancing round the maypole shows its self-assurance, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly missing' keeps A, P, L of maypole; 'dancing' turns MOB into OMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and poise under pressure, a close synonym for confidence.

clue.text: Informed about matches ref interrupts and spoils

indicators.note: about means turned round, so that word is read backwards

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be informed about it

indicators.note: interrupts says the referee's word breaks into the word for matches

parts.note: matches between teams are ties, as in cup ties

explanation.surface: A well-briefed pundit notes the referee's interruptions are ruining the games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the reversal and 'interrupts' the insertion; 'matches' are cup ties, not things to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that putrefies rots and goes off, which is what it means for food to spoil.

clue.text: Satisfactory beer served up for beast

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means placed upwards, so the beer's letters read backwards

parts.note: IPA is India pale ale, a beer

explanation.surface: A decent pint is poured out to feed an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses IPA to API, reading upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa related to the giraffe, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Joked with injured — taking name for the first time

indicators.note: taking signals one letter is brought in to stand in place of another
for the first says only the earlier of the two matching letters is swapped out

parts.note: battered means injured by blows

explanation.surface: Someone joked with a hurt friend, using a name for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'first time' is the first T of BATTERED, which N replaces. It reads as a single phrase, 'for the first time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To banter with someone is to exchange teasing remarks, so bantered means traded jokes with them.

clue.text: Holding on to snake — it's green

indicators.note: on to says the second piece is attached after the first in an across answer

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road winds
a holding is a piece of farmland, as in smallholding

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a snake and is told it is green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' is the noun, a tract of land, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm produces renewable electricity, and green is used of things that are environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Win back some alumni at talks

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Former students earn something back by giving talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden NIATTA, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to achieve or gain it, as one wins a prize or goal.

clue.text: Motivate stud

definitions.meaning: a projecting spike, like a stud on a boot or a spike on a rider's heel

explanation.surface: Encourage the stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stud' looks like a horse, which suits a spur, but it means a projecting spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur urges a horse onward, hence motivate; it is also a pointed projection like a stud.

clue.text: Superior story about eating on vacation

indicators.note: about says the word for story goes around the next piece

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' means emptied, keeping only the outside letters, and 'about' signals the wrap-around.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord, the superior to whom a vassal owed service.

clue.text: Rough brats surrounding playground I initially enjoyed

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like a description of the brats; it means approximate. A rec is a British public recreation ground.

clue.text: Villains' accents — not British

definitions.note: the apostrophe belongs to the surface; the plural villains matches the plural answer

indicators.note: not says the letter for British is left out of the word for accents

parts.note: brogues are regional accents, especially Irish

explanation.surface: The bad guys speak with accents that are not British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from BROGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogues are dishonest scoundrels, a straightforward synonym for villains.

clue.text: Perhaps boxers are knocked out — fighting without energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the fighting word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a nation fighting is at war

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' are shorts, not fighters, hence 'Perhaps'. 'without' puts WAR around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose men's pants, one example of underwear.

clue.text: Second edition on the subject of children

parts.note: RE means concerning, on the subject of
issue is a formal word for a person's children or offspring

explanation.surface: A revised book is published about children.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a book or record published again, a further edition after the first.

clue.text: Suspect lets alarm off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A criminal suspect sets the alarm off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for sensing that something is wrong, that is, to suspect trickery.

clue.text: Cruise, perhaps, features deckhand

parts.note: a feature is a full-length film
tar is old slang for a sailor or deckhand

explanation.surface: A sea voyage, perhaps, includes a sailor working on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruise is Tom Cruise, the actor, not a holiday at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise is a famous Hollywood actor, an example of a screen celebrity.

clue.text: Aide: ring and ask Biden to avoid extremes before heading to rally

indicators.note: before says the stripped words come ahead of the last letter
avoiding the extremes means dropping the first and last letters of each word
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A staffer is told to phone Joe Biden and ask him to stay off the fringes before the rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid extremes' strips ring, ask and Biden to IN, S and IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within an organisation, like an aide on a politician's staff.

clue.text: Trio regularly joining morning walk

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Three friends meet up for a morning stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about on foot, a kind of walking.

clue.text: Ring scrubber

definitions.meaning: a flat ring placed under a nut or bolt
someone or something that washes, a scrubber

explanation.surface: A ring cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is both a metal ring fitted to a bolt and a person who cleans by scrubbing.

clue.text: Watch wife charm Head

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal or charm
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Watch your wife charm the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' is the verb, to observe.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness an event is to see it happen, to watch it.

clue.text: Slow to drip compound

indicators.note: compound means combine and mix, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical compound is slow to drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, slow in movement.

clue.text: Tom & Jerry essentially reworked — it has an avant-garde aesthetic

parts.note: the ampersand is read as the word and

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, all but its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives ERR from Jerry; 'reworked' rearranges TOM + AND + ERR.

clue.text: Doctor, say, first to study sediment

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: first to says take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the solid residue that settles at the bottom of a liquid, that is, sediment.

clue.text: Small room love what Lloyd Webber plays

clue.text: Song starts to chart after release on vinyl at last
